title: Workplace harassment training requirements by country: Australia, the United States and Japan compared
description: How harassment prevention training duties compare in Australia, the United States and Japan: who must train, how often, what evidence, and what to localize.
shortAnswer: Workplace harassment training is handled very differently across Australia, the United States and Japan. Some US states, including California and New York, set explicit training mandates with fixed hours and intervals, but there is no federal mandate for private employers. Australia requires reasonable and proportionate prevention measures, with training expected by regulator guidance rather than prescribed by statute. Japan mandates prevention measures for all employers and makes training an effort duty.
keyTakeaways: Only some US states prescribe harassment training by hours and interval; California requires 2 hours for supervisors and 1 hour for other employees every two years, and New York requires annual training from every employer.

Australia's positive duty in section 47C of the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 is outcome based: the Australian Human Rights Commission expects ongoing, role tailored education, and says one off induction training has proven ineffective unless periodically reinforced.

Japan's Article 31 makes power harassment prevention measures mandatory for every employer; training to deepen workers' understanding is an effort duty under Article 32(2), and customer harassment duties apply from October 1, 2026.
This library does not yet document a harassment training duty for Portugal, the EU or the UAE, so those markets are not compared here.
A multinational can standardize a conduct framework and evidence model, but must localize definitions, hours, intervals and trigger events.

sections.heading: How do harassment training duties compare by market?

blocks.text: The three markets covered here sit on a spectrum from prescriptive to principle based. The United States is prescriptive state by state, Japan prescribes the prevention system but not the training, and Australia sets an outcome and leaves the means to the employer. The table summarizes each as at November 2026.

sections.heading: Which markets have an explicit harassment training duty?

blocks.text: Only certain US states impose an explicit, enforceable harassment training duty with defined hours or intervals. Australia and Japan require prevention, but neither statute makes training itself a hard obligation.

In the United States, the duty follows the employee's work location. As at November 2026, New York and Illinois require annual training from all employers; California requires training every two years at five or more employees; Delaware every two years at 50 or more employees in Delaware; Connecticut two hours within six months of hire at three or more employees; and Maine new hire training at 15 or more. There is no federal sexual harassment training mandate for private employers.

In Australia, section 47C(1) requires reasonable and proportionate measures to eliminate, as far as possible, workplace sexual harassment, sex discrimination and related conduct. It does not mention training. The Commission's Guidelines (August 2023) place education under Standard 3, Knowledge, and the Commission has had power to inquire into compliance and issue compliance notices since December 12, 2023. In practice an employer without education would struggle to show compliance, but the duty is to prevent, not to train.

In Japan, Article 31(1) obliges every employer to take employment management measures against power harassment, including a consultation system, and Article 32(2) asks employers to endeavor to deepen workers' understanding through training. There is no direct criminal penalty: under Article 42 the Minister can give advice, guidance and recommendations, and can publish the name of an employer that ignores a recommendation.

sections.heading: Do the markets mean the same thing by harassment?

blocks.text: No. The conduct each regime targets differs, which is the main reason a single global course cannot satisfy all three.

items: **Australia:** sexual harassment, sex discrimination, sex based harassment, hostile workplace environments on the ground of sex, and related victimization under section 47C(2); psychosocial rules separately cover bullying, harassment, high job demands and traumatic exposure.
**United States:** state mandates focus on sexual harassment; California's content must also include abusive conduct and harassment based on gender identity, gender expression and sexual orientation.

**Japan:** power harassment, defined by three elements that must all be met (behavior based on a superior relationship, beyond what is necessary and appropriate for the work, that harms the working environment); from October 1, 2026, customer harassment by customers, business partners and facility users, and sexual harassment of job seekers.

blocks.text: Japan's customer harassment rules and Australia's third party conduct coverage both extend training needs to customer facing staff, a group that US state mandates address only as ordinary employees.

sections.heading: What about Portugal, the EU and the UAE?

blocks.text: This library has no regulation page documenting a harassment training duty in Portugal, at EU level or in the UAE, so this comparison makes no claim about them. That is a gap in coverage, not a finding that no duty exists.

A multinational operating in those markets should confirm the local position with counsel before assuming the global program is sufficient, and should not read the absence of a page here as permission to exclude local staff from the group program.

sections.heading: What should a multinational standardize and what should it localize?

blocks.text: Standardize the conduct framework, the reporting pathway design and the evidence record; localize definitions, hours, intervals and anything a state or ministry prescribes. The strictest US state rules set a useful floor for evidence even where they do not apply.

blocks.text: An annual group default exceeds California's two year cycle and meets New York's and Illinois' annual cycle, so it rarely creates a gap. The localization risk lies in content and audiences, not frequency. A [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix) keyed to work location and role makes these overlays visible, and [setting refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) explains how to choose intervals that satisfy the strictest rule without overtraining.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry structures harassment obligations as concepts, roles and assessment points per jurisdiction before content is written, so a shared conduct framework carries local definitions and audience rules explicitly. Each completion record links to the content version and the obligation it evidences. See [compliance programs](/programs/compliance).

faqs.q: Is harassment training legally required in Australia?
faqs.a: Not by an explicit statutory training clause. Section 47C of the Sex Discrimination Act 1984 requires reasonable and proportionate measures to eliminate sexual harassment as far as possible. The Australian Human Rights Commission's Guidelines expect ongoing, role tailored education, and an employer without it would find compliance hard to demonstrate.

faqs.q: Does a non US company need to follow California or New York training rules?
faqs.a: Yes, for staff who work in those states. The US state duties follow the employee's work location, so a company headquartered anywhere must train its California or New York based employees. California counts employees anywhere toward its five employee threshold.

faqs.q: What changed in Japan in October 2026?
faqs.a: From October 1, 2026, customer harassment prevention measures became mandatory for all employers under new Article 33, with a training effort duty in Article 34(2). Sexual harassment of job seekers measures also became mandatory, and the power harassment provisions moved to Articles 31 and 32.

faqs.q: Is there a federal US harassment training requirement?
faqs.a: Not for private employers. Federal anti-discrimination law applies nationwide, but specific training mandates come from states such as California, New York, Illinois, Connecticut, Maine and Delaware, each with its own threshold and interval.
